questions.question: What kind of data is used to train a supervised learning model?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning uses labelled examples to learn how inputs relate to targets.
questions.quote: Supervised learning learns a mapping from inputs to targets using labelled training data.

questions.question: The test set should be used to train model parameters.
questions.explanation: The test set checks how the model performs on new data. It is not used to train the model.
questions.quote: The test set evaluates performance on unseen data and must not be used to train model parameters.

questions.question: What is overfitting, and how does it affect performance on training data and new data?
questions.answer: The model fits the training examples too closely. It does well on training data but poorly on new data.
questions.explanation: Good results on training data alone do not mean the model will do well on new data.
questions.quote: Overfitting occurs when a model fits training data too closely, performing well on training examples but poorly on unseen data.
